about.title: El Segundo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a power tool overheats, a car part snaps, a household item malfunctions without warning. In El Segundo, a small but tightly packed city bordered by industrial yards, aerospace facilities, and busy retail along Sepulveda Boulevard and Imperial Highway, people encounter consumer products, workplace equipment, and vehicle components every day. When one of those products causes an injury, California law generally allows an injured person to pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective, not whether anyone was careless. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result. We simply listen to what happened, gather the basics, and connect you with an independent attorney in our network who handles these cases on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why El Segundo Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: California often applies strict liability to defective products, so an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties an attorney may pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because the defect itself is central to these claims, keeping the product safe and unaltered can be important — an independent attorney can advise you on what to do with it right away.

items.question: I was hurt by a product bought at a store near Douglas Street — who can be held responsible?
items.answer: Under California's strict liability framework, responsibility can extend beyond just the manufacturer to include distributors and even the retailer that sold the product. An independent attorney can look at your specific situation and identify which parties may be involved. This is one reason product liability claims sometimes involve more than one defendant.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Many California product liability claims are based on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective, not on the manufacturer's conduct. An attorney can review whether your case fits a design defect, manufacturing defect, or failure-to-warn theory.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: It's generally wise to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without cleaning, repairing, or discarding it. The product itself is often key evidence in these claims. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on preserving it properly.
